reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Department creation, commission appointment, director, and staff
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 3, Effective 5-02-74). Creates the department of conservation headed by a four-member bipartisan conservation commission appointed by the governor with senate advice and consent under Article IV of the Missouri Constitution, and covers commission appointment of the director and approved appointment of assistants and employees.

headings.title: Type I transfer of commission powers and duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history/effective-date notes. Transfers all powers, duties, and functions of the conservation commission under chapters 252, 254, and others by type I transfer to the department of conservation.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1973 1st Ex. Sess. S.B. 1 § 3, Effective 5-02-74) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed creation of department, four-member bipartisan commission under Mo. Const. Art. IV, director, and approved staff in (1), and type I transfer of commission powers under chapters 252, 254, and others in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Discretionary restitution amounts for specified wildlife
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and history note (L. 2019 H.B. 260). Grants discretionary authority ('may order') in addition to section 252.040 penalties for a court to order state restitution within specified dollar ranges upon a finding of guilt for specified rule violations involving wild turkey, paddlefish, antlered white-tailed deer (excluding does), black bear, or elk.

headings.title: Transfer to state school moneys fund and distribution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs collected restitution moneys to the state school moneys fund under section 166.051 for public school distribution under section 163.031.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 (including subdivisions 1(1)–(4)) and history note (L. 2019 H.B. 260) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified discretionary ("may order") court restitution in addition to 252.040 penalties for specified species (wild turkey, paddlefish, antlered white-tailed deer excluding does, black bear, elk) in (1), and transfer to the section 166.051 state school moneys fund for section 163.031 distribution in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Motor vehicle travel areas and default speed limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1979 S.B. 163, A.L. 1993 H.B. 306, A.L. 1996 S.B. 661). Restricts motor vehicle operation on commission-owned, leased, or managed lands to designated roads, thoroughfares, or areas and sets a forty-five mph speed limit except as otherwise posted by the commission or established by other governmental authority.

headings.title: Restricted activities and utility or railroad entry exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Restricts listed recreational, vegetation, firearm, fire, and conveyance activities on commission lands and waters unless specifically authorized by the commission, and permits public utilities, rural electric cooperatives, and railroads to cut vegetation and construct/maintain services on easement or agreement areas with reasonable prior notification (waived for restoring essential utility services). Independent review revised title to reflect railroads and existing-agreement areas alongside public utilities and rural electric cooperatives.

headings.title: Prohibitions on discarding solid waste and off-site refuse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits discarding solid waste, garbage, refuse, or other materials on covered lands or waters, and bars placing off-site generated materials into solid waste receptacles located on those lands.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 1979 S.B. 163, A.L. 1993 H.B. 306, A.L. 1996 S.B. 661) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed designated travel areas and qualified 45-mph default speed limit in (1), restricted activities and prior-notice entry exceptions (with emergency restoration waiver) for public utilities, rural electric cooperatives, and railroads on easements or existing-agreement areas in (2), and solid waste and off-site receptacle prohibitions in (3). Retained titles (1) and (3); revised title (2) to include railroads alongside utilities.

headings.title: State officer status of chapter 590 certified agents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1981 S.B. 112, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1669, A.L. 1994 H.B. 1398, A.L. 1997 H.B. 424; Effective 7-07-97). Declares authorized commission agents certified as peace officers or instructors under chapter 590 to be officers of the state of Missouri in all courts with jurisdiction over state offenses.

headings.title: Peace officer authority on request and sheriff notification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Grants full peace officer authority when working with and at the special request of a county sheriff or city police chief or under highway patrol superintendent direction, subject to immediate notification of the county sheriff or designee when working in a county under this section and section 252.225 at the request of any agency other than the sheriff's department.

headings.title: Warrantless arrest on commission lands and incidental enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes warrantless probable-cause arrest for any state law violation on commission-owned, operated, managed, or leased lands, or on other lands when probable cause arises incidental to enforcing statutes the agents are authorized to enforce.

headings.title: Arrests for specified chapter 569 offenses and limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes, including footnote '*Section 569.067 was repealed by S.B. 491, 2014, effective 1-01-17.' Declares authorized agents peace officers for warrantless probable-cause arrests under sections 569.055, 569.065, 569.067*, 569.100, 569.120, 569.140, or 569.150, limited on non-commission lands by a landowner-complaint prerequisite for 569.100, 569.120, 569.140, and 569.150 and a bar on warrantless arrests for misdemeanors committed outside the agent's presence; source repeal footnote for 569.067 retained explicitly.

headings.title: Statewide on-view arrest for force risking death or serious injury
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Authorizes both chapter 590 certified peace officers and subsection 1 conservation commission agents to make warrantless on-view arrests anywhere in the state when observing physical force asserted to cause or create a substantial risk of death or serious injury. Independent review revised title from "life-threatening" to "risking death or serious injury" to match the full statutory threshold for both chapter 590 peace officers and subsection 1 agents.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–5 and all notes (L. 1981 S.B. 112 through A.L. 1997 H.B. 424; Effective 7-07-97; footnote "*Section 569.067 was repealed by S.B. 491, 2014, effective 1-01-17.") and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Checked chapter 590 state officer status in (1), request/highway-patrol-direction authority and immediate sheriff notification for non-sheriff requests under 252.085/252.225 in (2), commission-land and incidental warrantless arrests in (3), specified chapter 569 offenses with non-commission landowner-complaint and misdemeanor-presence limits plus retained 569.067 repeal footnote in (4), and statewide on-view arrest for peace officers and subsection 1 agents in (5). Retained titles (1)–(4); revised title (5) so it reflects risk of death or serious injury rather than only life-threatening force.

headings.title: Duty to permit package examination by commission agents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8953, A.L. 1945 p. 654 § 24). Imposes a duty on warehouses, merchants, common carriers, and their agents or employees to allow commission agents to examine suspected unlawfully possessed/transported wildlife packages or falsely labeled packages (retaining the source text where the second clause names 'warehouse or common carrier' without repeating 'merchant').

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for refusal and enforcement damage immunity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Establishes a misdemeanor penalty ($50 to $150 fine) for refusing permission to examine/open or impeding an agent or enforcement officer, and grants immunity from damages for searches, examinations, or seizures conducted in accordance with sections 252.010 to 252.240.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8953, A.L. 1945 p. 654 § 24) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified and explicitly preserved without silent repair subsection 1's source omission of "merchant" from the second clause ("in the possession of said warehouse or common carrier") after listing "warehouse, merchant, or common carrier" in the opening clause. Confirmed subsection 2 misdemeanor fine ($50–$150) and lawful-enforcement damage immunity under 252.010–252.240. Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Filing complaints without security for costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1945 p. 664 § 5). Authorizes commission agents, sheriffs, marshals, or their deputies to make complaints and commence violation proceedings without furnishing security for costs.

headings.title: Warrantless searches, wildlife seizures, and search warrant requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes warrantless search of listed hunting/fishing containers or boats and seizure of wildlife, subject to a daytime search-warrant requirement (with food-contamination precautions for cold storage locker plants) for occupied dwellings and adjacent outbuildings, cold storage plants, motor vehicles, or sealed freight/express cars, and directs circuit or associate circuit judges to issue warrants on sworn written probable-cause complaints.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for resisting search or warrant execution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Makes resisting such search or interfering with an agent or officer executing a search warrant a misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 1945 p. 664 § 5) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed complaint filing without cost security in (1), warrantless container/boat search, wildlife seizure, daytime warrant requirement (with cold storage contamination precaution), and judicial warrant issuance in (2), and misdemeanor penalty for resisting search or warrant execution in (3). All 3 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Fishway duties for dam owners, operators, and users
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 §§ 8938, 8939, A.L. 1945 p. 664 § 21), and cross-references (236.180, 236.230). Requires any person owning, operating, or using a dam across state waters to erect and maintain a commission-approved fishway or device for free fish passage (noting official catchline says 'Corporation owning dam' while subsections 1–3 apply to 'any person'). Independent review revised title to cover all three statutory parties ("owning, operating or using") while preserving the catchline-vs-body party difference.

headings.title: Commission-required fish hatcheries in lieu of fishways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2, history notes, and cross-references. Authorizes the commission, when fishways are deemed impractical or unnecessary, to require establishing and maintaining a commission-approved, commission-supervised fish hatchery to stock waters above and below the dam and allows the commission to take fish from the hatchery for public waters.

headings.title: Misdemeanor fine for fishway or hatchery violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3, history notes, and cross-references. Classifies violating this section or refusing to establish and maintain a required hatchery in lieu of a fishway as a misdemeanor fined $100 to $300 per violation.

headings.title: Corporate officer and agent duties and liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4, history notes, and cross-references. Places the section's corporate duties and liabilities upon the corporation's president, secretary, or manager in Missouri or any general or local agent.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4, history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 §§ 8938, 8939, A.L. 1945 p. 664 § 21), and cross-references (236.180, 236.230), and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified catchline ("Corporation owning dam") vs. body ("any person owning, operating or using any dam" in (1)–(3); corporate officers/agents in (4)). Revised title (1) to include dam owners, operators, and users; retained titles (2)–(4).

headings.title: Prohibition on explosives in waters and commission exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8926, A.L. 1945 p. 664 § 20). Prohibits placing explosives in state waters that may kill, injure, or destroy fish or taking fish by explosives, subject to the proviso permitting use only with commission permission and supervision.

headings.title: Felony fine or imprisonment penalties per offense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Classifies violations as a felony punishable per offense by a $200 to $1,000 fine, up to two years imprisonment in the state penitentiary, or both. Independent review revised title from "fine and imprisonment" to "fine or imprisonment" to match the statutory disjunctive ("or ... or both").

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8926, A.L. 1945 p. 664 § 20) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed prohibition on explosives in waters with commission permission/supervision proviso in (1), and felony penalty of fine, penitentiary imprisonment, or both per offense in (2). Retained title (1); revised title (2) from "and" to "or" to match the disjunctive statutory penalty.

headings.title: Statewide toll-free telephone service for violation reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1669, Effective 7-09-90). Grants permissive authority ('may maintain') for the department to operate a twenty-four-hour, single statewide toll-free telephone service to receive and record reports of violations of sections 252.010 to 252.240 and commission rules.

headings.title: Confidentiality of reports and authorized disclosure exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and notes. Makes reports and records confidential except for disclosures to appropriate department staff, grand juries/prosecutors/law enforcement for violation investigations or court proceedings, director-approved bona fide researchers (without identifying information), and the subject of the report.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for violations or unauthorized disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Makes violating this section or permitting or encouraging unauthorized dissemination of report or record information a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor penalty for filing false reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Classifies conviction for filing a false report as a class B misdemeanor with a permissive fine ('may be fined') up to five hundred dollars.

headings.title: Disclosure to report subjects and reporter identity redaction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires information about a report subject that is shared outside the department to also be disclosed to the subject when disseminated, while permitting the department to obscure or remove the reporter's identifying information.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–5 (including subdivisions 2(1)–(4)) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1990 H.B. 1669, Effective 7-09-90) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed permissive 24-hour statewide toll-free service in (1), confidentiality and four disclosure exceptions in (2), class A misdemeanor for violations or unauthorized disclosure in (3), class B misdemeanor and permissive fine up to $500 for false reports in (4), and mandatory disclosure to report subjects upon external release with permissive reporter redaction in (5). All 5 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Authorized recipients of individual permit records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (7) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 596). Lists seven categories of recipients entitled to access individual hunting, fishing, and trapping permit records (including address, phone, identifying characteristics, date of birth, and unique ID numbers).

headings.title: Permit-holder opt-out and closure of credit card numbers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes permit record information inaccessible to all other persons upon the permit holder's written request, and separately declares individual credit card numbers closed records exempt from release under section 610.021.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 (including subdivisions 1(1)–(7)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 596) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified seven authorized recipient categories for individual permit records in (1), and permit-holder written opt-out plus categorical closure of individual credit card numbers under section 610.021 in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Default class A misdemeanor under 252.010 to 252.240
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8967, A.L. 1945 p. 664 § 27, A.L. 1997 H.B. 424). Sets a class A misdemeanor default penalty for violations of sections 252.010 to 252.240 lacking other specific punishment and for related wildlife rule violations, explicitly qualified by 'except as provided in subsection 2 of this section'.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor for certain wildlife rule violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history notes. Classifies wildlife rule violations as a class B misdemeanor unless the rules pertain to sections 252.010 to 252.043 or sections 252.050 to 252.241 (preserving the exact statutory section ranges in the archived text). Independent review verified and explicitly records both statutory range discrepancies without repair: subsection 2 omits sections 252.044–252.049 (including section 252.045) between its 252.010–252.043 and 252.050–252.241 ranges, and cites an upper bound of 252.241 while subsection 1 cites 252.010 to 252.240.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 8967, A.L. 1945 p. 664 § 27, A.L. 1997 H.B. 424) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Explicitly verified and retained without silent repair the statutory section-range gap in subsection 2 (which cites 252.010 to 252.043 and 252.050 to 252.241, omitting 252.044–252.049 including 252.045) and the upper-bound mismatch between subsection 1 (252.010 to 252.240) and subsection 2 (252.241). Retained both drafted titles and expanded reviewNote (2) to record the gap.

headings.title: Prohibited endangered fish and wildlife activities and definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1972 H.B. 790 §§ 1, 2, 4, A.L. 1984 H.B. 1079). Prohibits importing, transporting, or selling endangered fish or wildlife or their parts, or selling/possessing with intent to sell articles made from them, and defines 'endangered species' by department rule and U.S. Department of the Interior lists. Independent review revised title to specify "endangered" fish and wildlife, parallel to subsection 2.

headings.title: Prohibited endangered plant activities, regulatory exception, and definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits exporting, transporting, or selling endangered plants or parts, or selling/possessing with intent to sell products made from them, qualified by 'unless authorized by regulation', and defines 'endangered species of plants' via department designations, federal ESA lists (Pub. L. 93-205), and CITES appendices.

headings.title: Sixty-day delayed effective date for filed rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Specifies that such department rule takes effect sixty days after filing with the secretary of state.

headings.title: Public zoo, lawful wildlife, and pre-1973 article exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Exempts publicly owned and operated zoos from the section and excludes legally acquired wildlife held under permit, wildlife legally taken in another state, and articles manufactured before January 1, 1973.

headings.title: Taking rare or endangered plants without owner permission
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 (commercial/export/transport) by prohibiting collecting, digging, or picking any rare or endangered plant without the property owner's permission.

headings.title: Class B misdemeanor penalty for violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Classifies any violation of the provisions of this section as a class B misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–6 and history note (L. 1972 H.B. 790 §§ 1, 2, 4, A.L. 1984 H.B. 1079) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified endangered fish/wildlife prohibitions and definition in (1), endangered plant prohibitions with regulatory exception and ESA/CITES definition in (2), 60-day delayed rule effective date in (3), public zoo, permitted/out-of-state lawful wildlife, and pre-1973 article exemptions in (4), taking rare/endangered plants without owner permission in (5), and class B misdemeanor penalty in (6). Revised title (1) to include "endangered"; retained titles (2)–(6).

headings.title: Prohibition during suspension, revocation, or denial of privileges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 306 § 1). Prohibits hunting or fishing during any period in which a hunting or fishing permit or privilege is suspended, revoked, or denied by a Missouri court or the conservation commission.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty for subsection 1 violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Classifies a violation of subsection 1 as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Penalties cumulative with other legal penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Specifies that penalties under this section are in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other penalties prescribed by law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–3 and history note (L. 1993 H.B. 306 § 1) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed ban on hunting or fishing while any permit or privilege is suspended, revoked, or denied by a Missouri court or commission in (1), class A misdemeanor penalty in (2), and cumulative penalty rule in (3). All 3 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Short title and river floodplain area designation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 S.B. 225). Establishes the 'Hunting Heritage Protection Areas Act' short title and designates hunting heritage protection areas as all land in the FEMA-designated one hundred-year flood plains of the Missouri and Mississippi rivers, as amended (subject to subsection 4 exclusions).

headings.title: Post-2007 tax increment financing prohibition and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Prohibits new TIF projects in hunting heritage protection areas after August 28, 2007 (in addition to section 99.847), with exceptions for pre-August 28, 2007 projects/districts (within 40% cost / 5% area expansion limits), flood/drainage protection and public infrastructure, and section 348.430 renewable fuel facilities (barring unrelated residential/commercial/industrial development).

headings.title: Protection of lawful firearm discharge and pre-2007 ordinances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides that discharge of firearms for lawful hunting, sporting, target shooting, and other lawful purposes shall not be prohibited in hunting heritage protection areas, subject to state and federal laws and local ordinances adopted before August 28, 2007. Major source catchline discrepancy retained explicitly: official Revisor catchline states 'discharge of firearms prohibited', contradicting the archived statutory text ('shall not be prohibited').

headings.title: Lands excluded from hunting heritage protection areas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and history note. Excludes from hunting heritage protection areas, notwithstanding subsection 1: 2000 Census urbanized areas of at least 50,000 population, land ever owned/used/operated by FERC-regulated entities, physical ports of commerce (not excess port authority land), specified home rule cities (>400,000 in >1 county) and cities not within a county, and land within one-half mile of interstate highways existing as of August 28, 2007.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 (including subdivisions 2(1)–(3) and 4(1)–(5)) and history note (L. 2007 S.B. 225) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed short title and FEMA 100-year Missouri/Mississippi River floodplain designation in (1), post-August 28, 2007 TIF ban and three exceptions in (2), explicit preservation of the major source contradiction in (3) where the official Revisor catchline says "discharge of firearms prohibited" while the statutory text states lawful firearm discharge "shall not be prohibited" subject to state/federal laws and pre-August 28, 2007 local ordinances, and five excluded land categories in (4). All 4 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Nonprofit, school, and public wild game service conditions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 596). Permits political subdivisions, elementary or secondary schools, and charitable, religious, fraternal, or other not-for-profit organizations to prepare or serve wild game without charge for the wild game in connection with organization meetings, fund-raising events, or free or reduced-rate meals for indigent persons. Independent review revised title to identify the eligible nonprofit, school, and political subdivision entities and the no-charge/event conditions.

headings.title: Required uninspected-game notice sign and section 537.115 exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires visible posting of a specified uninspected-game notice sign (at least 3/4-inch letters) at the dining area entrance, explicitly excepting venison donated or distributed pursuant to section 537.115.

headings.title: Donating legally taken wild game and labeling requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits donating, collecting, and transporting legally taken wild game to subsection 1 organizations and requires affixing the donor's name, address, and phone number to each package or container.

headings.title: Donation of property-damage game to approved charities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 3 by covering donation of wild game captured or killed to prevent private property damage (per wildlife rules) to department-approved charitable organizations and requiring the department to maintain an available list.

headings.title: Meaning of wild game and migratory bird exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Sets a non-exhaustive section-specific definition of 'wild game' under wildlife rules, expressly excluding federally regulated migratory birds.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–5 (including subdivisions 1(1)–(3)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 596) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Verified eligible political subdivision, school, and nonprofit entities and no-charge/event limits in (1), uninspected-game signage requirement and section 537.115 venison exception in (2), legally taken wild game donation and donor-labeling rules in (3), property-damage game donation to department-approved charities in (4), and non-exhaustive "wild game" definition excluding federally regulated migratory birds in (5). Revised title (1) to reflect eligible entities and conditions; retained titles (2)–(5).

headings.title: Authority to recruit, train, and use volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1997 H.B. 424). Grants permissive authority ('may') for the department of conservation to recruit, train, and utilize volunteers to supplement department-administered programs.

headings.title: Volunteer compliance with department rules and policies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires volunteers recruited, trained, or utilized by the department to comply with applicable department rules and policies.

headings.title: Department duties for managing and supporting volunteer programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and history note. Requires the department to provide program staff, develop citizen involvement opportunities, provide written volunteer rules, educate volunteers on duties and responsibilities, and recognize exceptional service.

headings.title: Authorized volunteer status and legal expense fund protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants unpaid employee status and legal expense fund and liability protections to volunteers or persons acting within designated scope and purpose when specifically authorized by the department director. Independent review revised title to reflect the director-authorization and scope-of-authority conditions for unpaid employee status and legal expense fund protection.

headings.title: Special assignment expense reimbursement and state vehicle use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Permits reimbursement of transportation and necessary expenses from regular appropriations for volunteers on department-determined necessary special assignments, and permits director-authorized volunteers to use state vehicles for department-related functions under paid-staff vehicle rules.

headings.title: Meaning of volunteer under this section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Defines 'volunteer' for this section as a person performing assigned department duties of free will without monetary or material compensation.

headings.title: Termination of volunteer service by department director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Authorizes the department director to terminate any person from service as a volunteer.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–7 (including subdivisions 3(1)–(5)) and history note (L. 1997 H.B. 424) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed permissive volunteer recruitment/use in (1), rule compliance in (2), five department management duties in (3), unpaid employee status and legal expense fund/liability protection conditioned on scope of authority and specific director authorization in (4), permissive special-assignment expense reimbursement and director-authorized state vehicle use in (5), section-specific definition in (6), and director termination authority in (7). Revised title (4) to reflect the authorization condition; retained titles (1)–(3) and (5)–(7).

headings.title: Authority to enter interstate wildlife violators compact
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 596). Grants permissive authority ('may enter') for the conservation commission to enter into an interstate wildlife violators compact with one or more states.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for compact implementation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may adopt') for the commission to adopt rules necessary to implement the compact.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 596) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed permissive commission authority to enter an interstate wildlife violators compact in (1) and adopt implementing rules in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Short title for sections 252.300 to 252.333
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 1). Designates sections 252.300 to 252.333 as 'The Missouri Economic Diversification and Afforestation Act of 1990'.

headings.title: Legislative intent of sections 252.300 to 252.333
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. States the legislative intent for a long-term integrated strategy addressing environmental, economic, and social programs for soil conservation, water and air quality, wildlife habitat, jobs, and reduced social problems.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 1) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed short title ("The Missouri Economic Diversification and Afforestation Act of 1990") in (1) and legislative intent for sections 252.300 to 252.333 in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Landowner incentive agreements and agroforestry use requirement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 4, A.L. 1993 S.B. 84, A.L. 2001 H.B. 904 merged with S.B. 462). Grants permissive authority for the director to enter enhancement-phase incentive payment agreements with individual landowners and requires recipients to use the land for agroforestry purposes under sections 252.300 to 252.333.

headings.title: Calculation of per-acre state incentive payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets the per-acre state incentive payment so that, combined with cash or in-kind net crop income from the land, it substantially equals the per-acre amount previously paid or payable under the federal conservation reserve program.

headings.title: Annual payment schedule for approved section 252.315 applications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the director to develop an annual state payment schedule if an application under section 252.315 is approved.

headings.title: Ten-year limit on enhancement-phase incentive payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Prohibits state payments to maintain enhancement-phase agroforestry land use after ten years have elapsed since the first incentive payment.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–4 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 4 through A.L. 2001 H.B. 904 merged with S.B. 462) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed permissive landowner enhancement-phase agreements and agroforestry use obligation in (1), federal CRP parity calculation in (2), annual payment schedule upon approved section 252.315 application in (3), and ten-year enhancement-phase payment limit in (4). All 4 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Written application contents, proposal plan, and tree standards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 6, A.L. 1993 S.B. 84, A.L. 2001 H.B. 904 merged with S.B. 462). Requires a written landowner application showing acreage, eligibility, and a detailed agroforestry proposal plan, and requires sufficient tree numbers consistent with practice standards.

headings.title: Application review, on-site inspection, cost-sharing, and appeal options
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers soil and land capability classification review, mandatory pre-decision on-site inspection and attestation, eligibility and cost-sharing determination (including in-kind and labor), and an aggrieved landowner's option upon non-approval to request a commission hearing within thirty days of notice or proceed under section 536.150 with Cole County venue.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 6 through A.L. 2001 H.B. 904 merged with S.B. 462) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed written application contents, proposal plan, and tree standards in (1), and soil/capability review, pre-decision on-site inspection and attestation, eligibility/cost-sharing determination, and 30-day commission hearing or section 536.150 Cole County appeal options in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Annual compliance inspection of participating agroforestry land
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 7). Requires annual inspection of participating land by a director's representative to verify continued compliance with sections 252.300 to 252.333 and practice specifications under applicable rules.

headings.title: Noncompliance notice, response options, appeals, and payment termination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers detailed noncompliance notice, thirty-day landowner response options (contesting via commission hearing or section 536.150 action in Cole County, or submitting a corrective proposal), non-suspension of payments while implementing an acceptable corrective proposal, and forfeiture of subsequent payments if unable or unwilling to correct acceptably.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 7) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed annual compliance inspection in (1), and detailed noncompliance notice, 30-day contest/corrective-proposal response, commission hearing or section 536.150 Cole County review, non-suspension during acceptable correction, and forfeiture of subsequent payments in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority, required consultation, and chapter 536 procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 9, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3, A.L. 2001 H.B. 904 merged with S.B. 462). Permits the director to promulgate rules for sections 252.300 to 252.333, mandates prior advice and comments from listed university, state, and private entities (and allows USDA/other consultation), and requires chapter 536 promulgation for effectiveness. Independent review also noted that the final chapter 536 effectiveness sentence refers to rules promulgated "under the authority of this chapter" while the opening sentence cites sections 252.300 to 252.333.

headings.title: Contracting with soil and water conservation division
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits the department of conservation to contract with the department of natural resources' division of soil and water conservation for administrative functions required under sections 252.300 to 252.333.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 9 through A.L. 2001 H.B. 904 merged with S.B. 462) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed permissive rulemaking for 252.300–252.333, mandatory university/agency/private consultation, and chapter 536 effectiveness clause (noting final sentence says "this chapter") in (1), and permissive contracting with DNR's division of soil and water conservation in (2). Both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Joint agroforestry report agencies and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 10). Directs the departments of conservation and economic development and the University of Missouri college of agriculture to jointly produce an agroforestry program report covering afforestation economic forecasts, business-development initiatives, wood/forestry product promotion, and job-growth initiatives.

headings.title: Report submission dates from 1996 through 2026
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Specifies submission to the governor and general assembly by January 31 in 1996, 2001, 2006, 2011, 2016, 2021, and 2026, retaining the archived statutory schedule without asserting post-2026 obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived text of subsections 1–2 (including subdivisions 1(1)–(4)) and history note (L. 1990 H.B. 1653 § 10) and verified source URL and all SHA-256 fingerprints. Confirmed joint reporting agencies and four required content items in (1), and archived January 31 submission schedule from 1996 through 2026 in (2) without asserting post-2026 duties. Both drafted titles retained.
